verses.1: From inside the fish Jonah prayed to the LORD his God.

verses.9: But I, with a song of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will make good. Salvation comes from the LORD."

verses.1: Then the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
verses.2: "Go to the great city of Nineveh and proclaim to it the message I give you."
verses.3: Jonah obeyed the word of the LORD and went to Nineveh. Now Nineveh was a very important city-a visit required three days.
verses.4: On the first day, Jonah started into the city. He proclaimed: "Forty more days and Nineveh will be overturned."
verses.5: The Ninevites believed God. They declared a fast, and all of them, from the greatest to the least, put on sackcloth.
verses.6: When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he rose from his throne, took off his royal robes, covered himself with sackcloth and sat down in the dust.
verses.7: Then he issued a proclamation in Nineveh: "By the decree of the king and his nobles: Do not let any man or beast, herd or flock, taste anything; do not let them eat or drink.
verses.8: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth. Let everyone call urgently on God. Let them give up their evil ways and their violence.
verses.9: Who knows? God may yet relent and with compassion turn from his fierce anger so that we will not perish."
verses.10: When God saw what they did and how they turned from their evil ways, he had compassion and did not bring upon them the destruction he had threatened.

verses.1: But Jonah was greatly displeased and became angry.
verses.2: He prayed to the LORD, "O LORD, is this not what I said when I was still at home? That is why I was so quick to flee to Tarshish. I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in love, a God who relents from sending calamity.
verses.3: Now, O LORD, take away my life, for it is better for me to die than to live."
verses.4: But the LORD replied, "Have you any right to be angry?"
verses.5: Jonah went out and sat down at a place east of the city. There he made himself a shelter, sat in its shade and waited to see what would happen to the city.
verses.6: Then the LORD God provided a vine and made it grow up over Jonah to give shade for his head to ease his discomfort, and Jonah was very happy about the vine.
verses.7: But at dawn the next day God provided a worm, which chewed the vine so that it withered.
verses.8: When the sun rose, God provided a scorching east wind, and the sun blazed on Jonah's head so that he grew faint. He wanted to die, and said, "It would be better for me to die than to live."
verses.9: But God said to Jonah, "Do you have a right to be angry about the vine?I do," he said. "I am angry enough to die."
verses.10: But the LORD said, "You have been concerned about this vine, though you did not tend it or make it grow. It sprang up overnight and died overnight.
verses.11: But Nineveh has more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and many cattle as well. Should I not be concerned about that great city?"

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
verses.2: Hear this, you elders; listen, all who live in the land. Has anything like this ever happened in your days or in the days of your forefathers?
verses.3: Tell it to your children, and let your children tell it to their children, and their children to the next generation.
verses.4: What the locust swarm has left the great locusts have eaten; what the great locusts have left the young locusts have eaten; what the young locusts have left other locusts have eaten.
verses.5: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine; wail because of the new wine, for it has been snatched from your lips.
verses.6: A nation has invaded my land, powerful and without number; it has the teeth of a lion, the fangs of a lioness.
verses.7: It has laid waste my vines and ruined my fig trees. It has stripped off their bark and thrown it away, leaving their branches white.
verses.8: Mourn like a virgin in sackcloth grieving for the husband of her youth.
verses.9: Grain offerings and drink offerings are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests are in mourning, those who minister before the LORD.
verses.10: The fields are ruined, the ground is dried up; the grain is destroyed, the new wine is dried up, the oil fails.
verses.11: Despair, you farmers, wail, you vine growers; grieve for the wheat and the barley, because the harvest of the field is destroyed.
verses.12: The vine is dried up and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, the palm and the apple tree- all the trees of the field-are dried up. Surely the joy of mankind is withered away.
verses.13: Put on sackcloth, O priests, and mourn; wail, you who minister before the altar. Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who minister before my God; for the grain offerings and drink offerings are withheld from the house of your God.
verses.14: Declare a holy fast; call a sacred assembly. Summon the elders and all who live in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
verses.15: Alas for that day! For the day of the LORD is near; it will come like destruction from the Almighty.
verses.16: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes- joy and gladness from the house of our God?
verses.17: The seeds are shriveled beneath the clods. The storehouses are in ruins, the granaries have been broken down, for the grain has dried up.
verses.18: How the cattle moan! The herds mill about because they have no pasture; even the flocks of sheep are suffering.
verses.19: To you, O LORD, I call, for fire has devoured the open pastures and flames have burned up all the trees of the field.
verses.20: Even the wild animals pant for you; the streams of water have dried up and fire has devoured the open pastures.

verses.12: "Even now," declares the LORD, "return to me with all your heart, with fasting and weeping and mourning."
verses.13: Rend your heart and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in love, and he relents from sending calamity.
verses.14: Who knows? He may turn and have pity and leave behind a blessing- grain offerings and drink offerings for the LORD your God.
verses.15: Blow the trumpet in Zion, declare a holy fast, call a sacred assembly.
verses.16: Gather the people, consecrate the assembly; bring together the elders, gather the children, those nursing at the breast. Let the bridegroom leave his room and the bride her chamber.
verses.17: Let the priests, who minister before the LORD, weep between the temple porch and the altar. Let them say, "Spare your people, O LORD. Do not make your inheritance an object of scorn, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
verses.18: Then the LORD will be jealous for his land and take pity on his people.
verses.19: The LORD will reply to them: "I am sending you grain, new wine and oil, enough to satisfy you fully; never again will I make you an object of scorn to the nations.
verses.20: "I will drive the northern army far from you, pushing it into a parched and barren land, with its front columns going into the eastern sea and those in the rear into the western sea. And its stench will go up; its smell will rise." Surely he has done great things.
verses.21: Be not afraid, O land; be glad and rejoice. Surely the LORD has done great things.
verses.22: Be not afraid, O wild animals, for the open pastures are becoming green. The trees are bearing their fruit; the fig tree and the vine yield their riches.
verses.23: Be glad, O people of Zion, rejoice in the LORD your God, for he has given you the autumn rains in righteousness. He sends you abundant showers, both autumn and spring rains, as before.
verses.24: The threshing floors will be filled with grain; the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
verses.25: "I will repay you for the years the locusts have eaten- the great locust and the young locust, the other locusts and the locust swarm - my great army that I sent among you.

verses.1: The words of Amos, one of the shepherds of Tekoa-what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
verses.2: He said: "The LORD roars from Zion and thunders from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds dry up, and the top of Carmel withers."
verses.3: This is what the LORD says: "For three sins of Damascus, even for four, I will not turn back my wrath. Because she threshed Gilead with sledges having iron teeth,
verses.4: I will send fire upon the house of Hazael that will consume the fortresses of Ben-Hadad.
verses.5: I will break down the gate of Damascus; I will destroy the king who is in the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter in Beth Eden. The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir," says the LORD.
verses.6: This is what the LORD says: "For three sins of Gaza, even for four, I will not turn back my wrath. Because she took captive whole communities and sold them to Edom,
verses.7: I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza that will consume her fortresses.
verses.8: I will destroy the king of Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, till the last of the Philistines is dead," says the Sovereign LORD.
verses.9: This is what the LORD says: "For three sins of Tyre, even for four, I will not turn back my wrath. Because she sold whole communities of captives to Edom, disregarding a treaty of brotherhood,
verses.10: I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre that will consume her fortresses."
verses.11: This is what the LORD says: "For three sins of Edom, even for four, I will not turn back my wrath. Because he pursued his brother with a sword, stifling all compassion, because his anger raged continually and his fury flamed unchecked,
verses.12: I will send fire upon Teman that will consume the fortresses of Bozrah."
verses.13: This is what the LORD says: "For three sins of Ammon, even for four, I will not turn back {my wrath}. Because he ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead in order to extend his borders,
verses.14: I will set fire to the walls of Rabbah that will consume her fortresses amid war cries on the day of battle, amid violent winds on a stormy day.
verses.15: Her king will go into exile, he and his officials together," says the LORD.

verses.1: Hear this word the LORD has spoken against you, O people of Israel-against the whole family I brought up out of Egypt:
verses.2: "You only have I chosen of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your sins."
verses.3: Do two walk together unless they have agreed to do so?
verses.4: Does a lion roar in the thicket when he has no prey? Does he growl in his den when he has caught nothing?
verses.5: Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground where no snare has been set? Does a trap spring up from the earth when there is nothing to catch?
verses.6: When a trumpet sounds in a city, do not the people tremble? When disaster comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?
verses.7: Surely the Sovereign LORD does nothing without revealing his plan to his servants the prophets.
verses.8: The lion has roared- who will not fear? The Sovereign LORD has spoken- who can but prophesy?

verses.14: "On the day I punish Israel for her sins, I will destroy the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
verses.15: I will tear down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses adorned with ivory will be destroyed and the mansions will be demolished," declares the LORD.

verses.1: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on Mount Samaria, you women who oppress the poor and crush the needy and say to your husbands, "Bring us some drinks!"
verses.2: The Sovereign LORD has sworn by his holiness: "The time will surely come when you will be taken away with hooks, the last of you with fishhooks.
verses.3: You will each go straight out through breaks in the wall, and you will be cast out toward Harmon, "declares the LORD.
verses.4: "Go to Bethel and sin; go to Gilgal and sin yet more. Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three years.
verses.5: Burn leavened bread as a thank offering and brag about your freewill offerings- boast about them, you Israelites, for this is what you love to do," declares the Sovereign LORD.
verses.6: "I gave you empty stomachs in every city and lack of bread in every town, yet you have not returned to me," declares the LORD.
verses.7: "I also withheld rain from you when the harvest was still three months away. I sent rain on one town, but withheld it from another. One field had rain; another had none and dried up.
verses.8: People staggered from town to town for water but did not get enough to drink, yet you have not returned to me," declares the LORD.
verses.9: "Many times I struck your gardens and vineyards, I struck them with blight and mildew. Locusts devoured your fig and olive trees, yet you have not returned to me," declares the LORD.
verses.10: "I sent plagues among you as I did to Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses. I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camps, yet you have not returned to me," declares the LORD.
verses.11: "I overthrew some of you as I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah. You were like a burning stick snatched from the fire, yet you have not returned to me," declares the LORD.
verses.12: "Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel, and because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel."
verses.13: He who forms the mountains, creates the wind, and reveals his thoughts to man, he who turns dawn to darkness, and treads the high places of the earth- the LORD God Almighty is his name.

verses.1: Hear this word, O house of Israel, this lament I take up concerning you:
verses.2: "Fallen is Virgin Israel, never to rise again, deserted in her own land, with no one to lift her up."
verses.3: This is what the Sovereign LORD says: "The city that marches out a thousand strong for Israel will have only a hundred left; the town that marches out a hundred strong will have only ten left."
verses.4: This is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: "Seek me and live;
verses.5: do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, do not journey to Beersheba. For Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will be reduced to nothing. "
verses.6: Seek the LORD and live, or he will sweep through the house of Joseph like a fire; it will devour, and Bethel will have no one to quench it.
verses.7: You who turn justice into bitterness and cast righteousness to the ground
verses.8: (he who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns blackness into dawn and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the land- the LORD is his name-
verses.9: he flashes destruction on the stronghold and brings the fortified city to ruin),
verses.10: you hate the one who reproves in court and despise him who tells the truth.
verses.11: You trample on the poor and force him to give you grain. Therefore, though you have built stone mansions, you will not live in them; though you have planted lush vineyards, you will not drink their wine.
verses.12: For I know how many are your offenses and how great your sins. You oppress the righteous and take bribes and you deprive the poor of justice in the courts.
verses.13: Therefore the prudent man keeps quiet in such times, for the times are evil.
verses.14: Seek good, not evil, that you may live. Then the LORD God Almighty will be with you, just as you say he is.
verses.15: Hate evil, love good; maintain justice in the courts. Perhaps the LORD God Almighty will have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.

verses.1: Woe to you who are complacent in Zion, and to you who feel secure on Mount Samaria, you notable men of the foremost nation, to whom the people of Israel come!
verses.2: Go to Calneh and look at it; go from there to great Hamath, and then go down to Gath in Philistia. Are they better off than your two kingdoms? Is their land larger than yours?
verses.3: You put off the evil day and bring near a reign of terror.
verses.4: You lie on beds inlaid with ivory and lounge on your couches. You dine on choice lambs and fattened calves.
verses.5: You strum away on your harps like David and improvise on musical instruments.
verses.6: You drink wine by the bowlful and use the finest lotions, but you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
verses.7: Therefore you will be among the first to go into exile; your feasting and lounging will end.
verses.8: The Sovereign LORD has sworn by himself-the LORD God Almighty declares: "I abhor the pride of Jacob and detest his fortresses; I will deliver up the city and everything in it."
verses.9: If ten men are left in one house, they too will die.
verses.10: And if a relative who is to burn the bodies comes to carry them out of the house and asks anyone still hiding there, "Is anyone with you?" and he says, "No," then he will say, "Hush! We must not mention the name of the LORD."
verses.11: For the LORD has given the command, and he will smash the great house into pieces and the small house into bits.

verses.1: I saw the Lord standing by the altar, and he said: "Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake. Bring them down on the heads of all the people; those who are left I will kill with the sword. Not one will get away, none will escape.
verses.2: Though they dig down to the depths of the grave, from there my hand will take them. Though they climb up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
verses.3: Though they hide themselves on the top of Carmel, there I will hunt them down and seize them. Though they hide from me at the bottom of the sea, there I will command the serpent to bite them.
verses.4: Though they are driven into exile by their enemies, there I will command the sword to slay them. I will fix my eyes upon them for evil and not for good."
verses.5: The Lord, the LORD Almighty, he who touches the earth and it melts, and all who live in it mourn- the whole land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt-
verses.6: he who builds his lofty palace in the heavens and sets its foundation on the earth, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out over the face of the land- the LORD is his name.
verses.7: "Are not you Israelites the same to me as the Cushites?" declares the LORD. "Did I not bring Israel up from Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor and the Arameans from Kir?
verses.8: "Surely the eyes of the Sovereign LORD are on the sinful kingdom. I will destroy it from the face of the earth- yet I will not totally destroy the house of Jacob," declares the LORD.
verses.9: "For I will give the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations as grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble will reach the ground.
verses.10: All the sinners among my people will die by the sword, all those who say, 'Disaster will not overtake or meet us.'
verses.11: "In that day I will restore David's fallen tent. I will repair its broken places, restore its ruins, and build it as it used to be,
verses.12: so that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear my name, "declares the LORD, who will do these things.
verses.13: "The days are coming," declares the LORD, "when the reaper will be overtaken by the plowman and the planter by the one treading grapes. New wine will drip from the mountains and flow from all the hills.
verses.14: I will bring back my exiled people Israel; they will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
verses.15: I will plant Israel in their own land, never again to be uprooted from the land I have given them," says the LORD your God.

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash king of Israel:
verses.2: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to him, "Go, take to yourself an adulterous wife and children of unfaithfulness, because the land is guilty of the vilest adultery in departing from the LORD."
verses.3: So he married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.4: Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call him Jezreel, because I will soon punish the house of Jehu for the massacre at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
verses.5: In that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.6: Gomer conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call her Lo-Ruhamah, for I will no longer show love to the house of Israel, that I should at all forgive them.
verses.7: Yet I will show love to the house of Judah; and I will save them-not by bow, sword or battle, or by horses and horsemen, but by the LORD their God."
verses.8: After she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, Gomer had another son.
verses.9: Then the LORD said, "Call him Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people, and I am not your God.
verses.10: "Yet the Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' they will be called 'sons of the living God.'
verses.11: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be reunited, and they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

verses.1: "Say of your brothers, 'My people,' and of your sisters, 'My loved one.'
verses.2: "Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adulterous look from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.
verses.3: Otherwise I will strip her naked and make her as bare as on the day she was born; I will make her like a desert, turn her into a parched land, and slay her with thirst.
verses.4: I will not show my love to her children, because they are the children of adultery.
verses.5: Their mother has been unfaithful and has conceived them in disgrace. She said, 'I will go after my lovers, who give me my food and my water, my wool and my linen, my oil and my drink.'
verses.6: Therefore I will block her path with thornbushes; I will wall her in so that she cannot find her way.
verses.7: She will chase after her lovers but not catch them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my husband as at first, for then I was better off than now.'
verses.8: She has not acknowledged that I was the one who gave her the grain, the new wine and oil, who lavished on her the silver and gold- which they used for Baal.
verses.9: "Therefore I will take away my grain when it ripens, and my new wine when it is ready. I will take back my wool and my linen, intended to cover her nakedness.
verses.10: So now I will expose her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers; no one will take her out of my hands.
verses.11: I will stop all her celebrations: her yearly festivals, her New Moons, her Sabbath days-all her appointed feasts.
verses.12: I will ruin her vines and her fig trees, which she said were her pay from her lovers; I will make them a thicket, and wild animals will devour them.
verses.13: I will punish her for the days she burned incense to the Baals; she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot," declares the LORD.
verses.14: "Therefore I am now going to allure her; I will lead her into the desert and speak tenderly to her.
verses.15: There I will give her back her vineyards, and will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will sing as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
verses.16: "In that day," declares the LORD, "you will call me 'my husband'; you will no longer call me 'my master. '
verses.17: I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips; no longer will their names be invoked.
verses.18: In that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that move along the ground. Bow and sword and battle I will abolish from the land, so that all may lie down in safety.
verses.19: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion.
verses.20: I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will acknowledge the LORD.
verses.21: "In that day I will respond," declares the LORD - "I will respond to the skies, and they will respond to the earth;
verses.22: and the earth will respond to the grain, the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
verses.23: I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show my love to the one I called 'Not my loved one. 'I will say to those called 'Not my people, You are my people'; and they will say, 'You are my God.'"

verses.1: The LORD said to me, "Go, show your love to your wife again, though she is loved by another and is an adulteress. Love her as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love the sacred raisin cakes."
verses.2: So I bought her for fifteen shekels of silver and about a homer and a lethek of barley.
verses.3: Then I told her, "You are to live with me many days; you must not be a prostitute or be intimate with any man, and I will live with you."
verses.4: For the Israelites will live many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or sacred stones, without ephod or idol.
verses.5: Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his blessings in the last days.

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and during the reign of Jeroboam son of Jehoash king of Israel:
verses.2: When the LORD began to speak through Hosea, the LORD said to him, "Go, take to yourself an adulterous wife and children of unfaithfulness, because the land is guilty of the vilest adultery in departing from the LORD."
verses.3: So he married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.4: Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call him Jezreel, because I will soon punish the house of Jehu for the massacre at Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of Israel.
verses.5: In that day I will break Israel's bow in the Valley of Jezreel."
verses.6: Gomer conceived again and gave birth to a daughter. Then the LORD said to Hosea, "Call her Lo-Ruhamah, for I will no longer show love to the house of Israel, that I should at all forgive them.
verses.7: Yet I will show love to the house of Judah; and I will save them-not by bow, sword or battle, or by horses and horsemen, but by the LORD their God."
verses.8: After she had weaned Lo-Ruhamah, Gomer had another son.
verses.9: Then the LORD said, "Call him Lo-Ammi, for you are not my people, and I am not your God.
verses.10: "Yet the Israelites will be like the sand on the seashore, which cannot be measured or counted. In the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' they will be called 'sons of the living God.'
verses.11: The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be reunited, and they will appoint one leader and will come up out of the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.

verses.1: "Say of your brothers, 'My people,' and of your sisters, 'My loved one.'
verses.2: "Rebuke your mother, rebuke her, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove the adulterous look from her face and the unfaithfulness from between her breasts.
verses.3: Otherwise I will strip her naked and make her as bare as on the day she was born; I will make her like a desert, turn her into a parched land, and slay her with thirst.
verses.4: I will not show my love to her children, because they are the children of adultery.
verses.5: Their mother has been unfaithful and has conceived them in disgrace. She said, 'I will go after my lovers, who give me my food and my water, my wool and my linen, my oil and my drink.'
verses.6: Therefore I will block her path with thornbushes; I will wall her in so that she cannot find her way.
verses.7: She will chase after her lovers but not catch them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my husband as at first, for then I was better off than now.'
verses.8: She has not acknowledged that I was the one who gave her the grain, the new wine and oil, who lavished on her the silver and gold- which they used for Baal.
verses.9: "Therefore I will take away my grain when it ripens, and my new wine when it is ready. I will take back my wool and my linen, intended to cover her nakedness.
verses.10: So now I will expose her lewdness before the eyes of her lovers; no one will take her out of my hands.
verses.11: I will stop all her celebrations: her yearly festivals, her New Moons, her Sabbath days-all her appointed feasts.
verses.12: I will ruin her vines and her fig trees, which she said were her pay from her lovers; I will make them a thicket, and wild animals will devour them.
verses.13: I will punish her for the days she burned incense to the Baals; she decked herself with rings and jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot," declares the LORD.
verses.14: "Therefore I am now going to allure her; I will lead her into the desert and speak tenderly to her.
verses.15: There I will give her back her vineyards, and will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will sing as in the days of her youth, as in the day she came up out of Egypt.
verses.16: "In that day," declares the LORD, "you will call me 'my husband'; you will no longer call me 'my master. '
verses.17: I will remove the names of the Baals from her lips; no longer will their names be invoked.
verses.18: In that day I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that move along the ground. Bow and sword and battle I will abolish from the land, so that all may lie down in safety.
verses.19: I will betroth you to me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in love and compassion.
verses.20: I will betroth you in faithfulness, and you will acknowledge the LORD.
verses.21: "In that day I will respond," declares the LORD - "I will respond to the skies, and they will respond to the earth;
verses.22: and the earth will respond to the grain, the new wine and oil, and they will respond to Jezreel.
verses.23: I will plant her for myself in the land; I will show my love to the one I called 'Not my loved one. 'I will say to those called 'Not my people, You are my people'; and they will say, 'You are my God.'"

verses.1: Hear the word of the LORD, you Israelites, because the LORD has a charge to bring against you who live in the land: "There is no faithfulness, no love, no acknowledgment of God in the land.
verses.2: There is only cursing, lying and murder, stealing and adultery; they break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
verses.3: Because of this the land mourns, and all who live in it waste away; the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the fish of the sea are dying.
verses.4: "But let no man bring a charge, let no man accuse another, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.
verses.5: You stumble day and night, and the prophets stumble with you. So I will destroy your mother-
verses.6: my people are destroyed from lack of knowledge. "Because you have rejected knowledge, I also reject you as my priests; because you have ignored the law of your God, I also will ignore your children.
verses.7: The more the priests increased, the more they sinned against me; they exchanged their Glory for something disgraceful.
verses.8: They feed on the sins of my people and relish their wickedness.
verses.9: And it will be: Like people, like priests. I will punish both of them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
verses.10: "They will eat but not have enough; they will engage in prostitution but not increase, because they have deserted the LORD to give themselves
verses.11: to prostitution, to old wine and new, which take away the understanding
verses.12: of my people. They consult a wooden idol and are answered by a stick of wood. A spirit of prostitution leads them astray; they are unfaithful to their God.
verses.13: They sacrifice on the mountaintops and burn offerings on the hills, under oak, poplar and terebinth, where the shade is pleasant. Therefore your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law to adultery.
verses.14: "I will not punish your daughters when they turn to prostitution, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because the men themselves consort with harlots and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes- a people without understanding will come to ruin!
verses.15: "Though you commit adultery, O Israel, let not Judah become guilty. "Do not go to Gilgal; do not go up to Beth Aven. And do not swear, 'As surely as the LORD lives!'
verses.16: The Israelites are stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. How then can the LORD pasture them like lambs in a meadow?
verses.17: Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
verses.18: Even when their drinks are gone, they continue their prostitution; their rulers dearly love shameful ways.
verses.19: A whirlwind will sweep them away, and their sacrifices will bring them shame.

verses.1: "Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, you Israelites! Listen, O royal house! This judgment is against you: You have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread out on Tabor.
verses.2: The rebels are deep in slaughter. I will discipline all of them.
verses.3: I know all about Ephraim; Israel is not hidden from me. Ephraim, you have now turned to prostitution; Israel is corrupt.
verses.4: "Their deeds do not permit them to return to their God. A spirit of prostitution is in their heart; they do not acknowledge the LORD.
verses.5: Israel's arrogance testifies against them; the Israelites, even Ephraim, stumble in their sin; Judah also stumbles with them.
verses.6: When they go with their flocks and herds to seek the LORD, they will not find him; he has withdrawn himself from them.
verses.7: They are unfaithful to the LORD; they give birth to illegitimate children. Now their New Moon festivals will devour them and their fields.
verses.8: "Sound the trumpet in Gibeah, the horn in Ramah. Raise the battle cry in Beth Aven; lead on, O Benjamin.
verses.9: Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of reckoning. Among the tribes of Israel I proclaim what is certain.
verses.10: Judah's leaders are like those who move boundary stones. I will pour out my wrath on them like a flood of water.
verses.11: Ephraim is oppressed, trampled in judgment, intent on pursuing idols.
verses.12: I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the people of Judah.
verses.13: "When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his sores, then Ephraim turned to Assyria, and sent to the great king for help. But he is not able to cure you, not able to heal your sores.
verses.14: For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a great lion to Judah. I will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, with no one to rescue them.
verses.15: Then I will go back to my place until they admit their guilt. And they will seek my face; in their misery they will earnestly seek me."

verses.1: "Come, let us return to the LORD. He has torn us to pieces but he will heal us; he has injured us but he will bind up our wounds.
verses.2: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will restore us, that we may live in his presence.
verses.3: Let us acknowledge the LORD; let us press on to acknowledge him. As surely as the sun rises, he will appear; he will come to us like the winter rains, like the spring rains that water the earth."
verses.4: "What can I do with you, Ephraim? What can I do with you, Judah? Your love is like the morning mist, like the early dew that disappears.
verses.5: Therefore I cut you in pieces with my prophets, I killed you with the words of my mouth; my judgments flashed like lightning upon you.
verses.6: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and acknowledgment of God rather than burnt offerings.
verses.7: Like Adam, they have broken the covenant- they were unfaithful to me there.
verses.8: Gilead is a city of wicked men, stained with footprints of blood.
verses.9: As marauders lie in ambush for a man, so do bands of priests; they murder on the road to Shechem, committing shameful crimes.
verses.10: I have seen a horrible thing in the house of Israel. There Ephraim is given to prostitution and Israel is defiled.
verses.11: "Also for you, Judah, a harvest is appointed. "Whenever I would restore the fortunes of my people,

verses.1: whenever I would heal Israel, the sins of Ephraim are exposed and the crimes of Samaria revealed. They practice deceit, thieves break into houses, bandits rob in the streets;
verses.2: but they do not realize that I remember all their evil deeds. Their sins engulf them; they are always before me.
verses.3: "They delight the king with their wickedness, the princes with their lies.
verses.4: They are all adulterers, burning like an oven whose fire the baker need not stir from the kneading of the dough till it rises.
verses.5: On the day of the festival of our king the princes become inflamed with wine, and he joins hands with the mockers.
verses.6: Their hearts are like an oven; they approach him with intrigue. Their passion smolders all night; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
verses.7: All of them are hot as an oven; they devour their rulers. All their kings fall, and none of them calls on me.
verses.8: "Ephraim mixes with the nations; Ephraim is a flat cake not turned over.
verses.9: Foreigners sap his strength, but he does not realize it. His hair is sprinkled with gray, but he does not notice.
verses.10: Israel's arrogance testifies against him, but despite all this he does not return to the LORD his God or search for him.
verses.11: "Ephraim is like a dove, easily deceived and senseless- now calling to Egypt, now turning to Assyria.
verses.12: When they go, I will throw my net over them; I will pull them down like birds of the air. When I hear them flocking together, I will catch them.
verses.13: Woe to them, because they have strayed from me! Destruction to them, because they have rebelled against me! I long to redeem them but they speak lies against me.
verses.14: They do not cry out to me from their hearts but wail upon their beds. They gather together for grain and new wine but turn away from me.
verses.15: I trained them and strengthened them, but they plot evil against me.
verses.16: They do not turn to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their leaders will fall by the sword because of their insolent words. For this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt.

verses.1: "Put the trumpet to your lips! An eagle is over the house of the LORD because the people have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
verses.2: Israel cries out to me, 'O our God, we acknowledge you!'
verses.3: But Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
verses.4: They set up kings without my consent; they choose princes without my approval. With their silver and gold they make idols for themselves to their own destruction.
verses.5: Throw out your calf-idol, O Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of purity?
verses.6: They are from Israel! This calf-a craftsman has made it; it is not God. It will be broken in pieces, that calf of Samaria.
verses.7: "They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind. The stalk has no head; it will produce no flour. Were it to yield grain, foreigners would swallow it up.
verses.8: Israel is swallowed up; now she is among the nations like a worthless thing.
verses.9: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has sold herself to lovers.
verses.10: Although they have sold themselves among the nations, I will now gather them together. They will begin to waste away under the oppression of the mighty king.
verses.11: "Though Ephraim built many altars for sin offerings, these have become altars for sinning.
verses.12: I wrote for them the many things of my law, but they regarded them as something alien.
verses.13: They offer sacrifices given to me and they eat the meat, but the LORD is not pleased with them. Now he will remember their wickedness and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
verses.14: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has fortified many towns. But I will send fire upon their cities that will consume their fortresses."

verses.7: "They sow the wind and reap the whirlwind. The stalk has no head; it will produce no flour. Were it to yield grain, foreigners would swallow it up.
verses.8: Israel is swallowed up; now she is among the nations like a worthless thing.
verses.9: For they have gone up to Assyria like a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has sold herself to lovers.
verses.10: Although they have sold themselves among the nations, I will now gather them together. They will begin to waste away under the oppression of the mighty king.
verses.11: "Though Ephraim built many altars for sin offerings, these have become altars for sinning.
verses.12: I wrote for them the many things of my law, but they regarded them as something alien.
verses.13: They offer sacrifices given to me and they eat the meat, but the LORD is not pleased with them. Now he will remember their wickedness and punish their sins: They will return to Egypt.
verses.14: Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces; Judah has fortified many towns. But I will send fire upon their cities that will consume their fortresses."

verses.1: Do not rejoice, O Israel; do not be jubilant like the other nations. For you have been unfaithful to your God; you love the wages of a prostitute at every threshing floor.
verses.2: Threshing floors and winepresses will not feed the people; the new wine will fail them.
verses.3: They will not remain in the LORD's land; Ephraim will return to Egypt and eat unclean food in Assyria.
verses.4: They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, nor will their sacrifices please him. Such sacrifices will be to them like the bread of mourners; all who eat them will be unclean. This food will be for themselves; it will not come into the temple of the LORD.
verses.5: What will you do on the day of your appointed feasts, on the festival days of the LORD?
verses.6: Even if they escape from destruction, Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Their treasures of silver will be taken over by briers, and thorns will overrun their tents.
verses.7: The days of punishment are coming, the days of reckoning are at hand. Let Israel know this. Because your sins are so many and your hostility so great, the prophet is considered a fool, the inspired man a maniac.
verses.8: The prophet, along with my God, is the watchman over Ephraim, yet snares await him on all his paths, and hostility in the house of his God.
verses.9: They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their wickedness and punish them for their sins.
verses.10: "When I found Israel, it was like finding grapes in the desert; when I saw your fathers, it was like seeing the early fruit on the fig tree. But when they came to Baal Peor, they consecrated themselves to that shameful idol and became as vile as the thing they loved.
verses.11: Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird- no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
verses.12: Even if they rear children, I will bereave them of every one. Woe to them when I turn away from them!
verses.13: I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a pleasant place. But Ephraim will bring out their children to the slayer."
verses.14: Give them, O LORD - what will you give them? Give them wombs that miscarry and breasts that are dry.
verses.15: "Because of all their wickedness in Gilgal, I hated them there. Because of their sinful deeds, I will drive them out of my house. I will no longer love them; all their leaders are rebellious.
verses.16: Ephraim is blighted, their root is withered, they yield no fruit. Even if they bear children, I will slay their cherished offspring."
verses.17: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed him; they will be wanderers among the nations.

verses.1: Israel was a spreading vine; he brought forth fruit for himself. As his fruit increased, he built more altars; as his land prospered, he adorned his sacred stones.
verses.2: Their heart is deceitful, and now they must bear their guilt. The LORD will demolish their altars and destroy their sacred stones.
verses.3: Then they will say, "We have no king because we did not revere the LORD. But even if we had a king, what could he do for us?"
verses.4: They make many promises, take false oaths and make agreements; therefore lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds in a plowed field.
verses.5: The people who live in Samaria fear for the calf-idol of Beth Aven. Its people will mourn over it, and so will its idolatrous priests, those who had rejoiced over its splendor, because it is taken from them into exile.
verses.6: It will be carried to Assyria as tribute for the great king. Ephraim will be disgraced; Israel will be ashamed of its wooden idols.
verses.7: Samaria and its king will float away like a twig on the surface of the waters.
verses.8: The high places of wickedness will be destroyed- it is the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistles will grow up and cover their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall on us!"
verses.9: "Since the days of Gibeah, you have sinned, O Israel, and there you have remained. Did not war overtake the evildoers in Gibeah?
verses.10: When I please, I will punish them; nations will be gathered against them to put them in bonds for their double sin.
verses.11: Ephraim is a trained heifer that loves to thresh; so I will put a yoke on her fair neck. I will drive Ephraim, Judah must plow, and Jacob must break up the ground.
verses.12: Sow for yourselves righteousness, reap the fruit of unfailing love, and break up your unplowed ground; for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and showers righteousness on you.
verses.13: But you have planted wickedness, you have reaped evil, you have eaten the fruit of deception. Because you have depended on your own strength and on your many warriors,
verses.14: the roar of battle will rise against your people, so that all your fortresses will be devastated- as Shalman devastated Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to the ground with their children.
verses.15: Thus will it happen to you, O Bethel, because your wickedness is great. When that day dawns, the king of Israel will be completely destroyed.

verses.1: "When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
verses.2: But the more I called Israel, the further they went from me. They sacrificed to the Baals and they burned incense to images.
verses.3: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms; but they did not realize it was I who healed them.
verses.4: I led them with cords of human kindness, with ties of love; I lifted the yoke from their neck and bent down to feed them.
verses.5: "Will they not return to Egypt and will not Assyria rule over them because they refuse to repent?
verses.6: Swords will flash in their cities, will destroy the bars of their gates and put an end to their plans.
verses.7: My people are determined to turn from me. Even if they call to the Most High, he will by no means exalt them.
verses.8: "How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I treat you like Admah? How can I make you like Zeboiim? My heart is changed within me; all my compassion is aroused.
verses.9: I will not carry out my fierce anger, nor will I turn and devastate Ephraim. For I am God, and not man- the Holy One among you. I will not come in wrath.
verses.10: They will follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
verses.11: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from Assyria. I will settle them in their homes," declares the LORD.
verses.12: Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, the house of Israel with deceit. And Judah is unruly against God, even against the faithful Holy One.

verses.1: Ephraim feeds on the wind; he pursues the east wind all day and multiplies lies and violence. He makes a treaty with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.
verses.2: The LORD has a charge to bring against Judah; he will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
verses.3: In the womb he grasped his brother's heel; as a man he struggled with God.
verses.4: He struggled with the angel and overcame him; he wept and begged for his favor. He found him at Bethel and talked with him there-
verses.5: the LORD God Almighty, the LORD is his name of renown!
verses.6: But you must return to your God; maintain love and justice, and wait for your God always.
verses.7: The merchant uses dishonest scales; he loves to defraud.
verses.8: Ephraim boasts, "I am very rich; I have become wealthy. With all my wealth they will not find in me any iniquity or sin."
verses.9: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt; I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of your appointed feasts.
verses.10: I spoke to the prophets, gave them many visions and told parables through them."
verses.11: Is Gilead wicked? Its people are worthless! Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Their altars will be like piles of stones on a plowed field.
verses.12: Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served to get a wife, and to pay for her he tended sheep.
verses.13: The LORD used a prophet to bring Israel up from Egypt, by a prophet he cared for him.
verses.14: But Ephraim has bitterly provoked him to anger; his Lord will leave upon him the guilt of his bloodshed and will repay him for his contempt.

verses.1: When Ephraim spoke, men trembled; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty of Baal worship and died.
verses.2: Now they sin more and more; they make idols for themselves from their silver, cleverly fashioned images, all of them the work of craftsmen. It is said of these people, "They offer human sacrifice and kiss the calf-idols."
verses.3: Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the early dew that disappears, like chaff swirling from a threshing floor, like smoke escaping through a window.
verses.4: "But I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt. You shall acknowledge no God but me, no Savior except me.
verses.5: I cared for you in the desert, in the land of burning heat.
verses.6: When I fed them, they were satisfied; when they were satisfied, they became proud; then they forgot me.
verses.7: So I will come upon them like a lion, like a leopard I will lurk by the path.
verses.8: Like a bear robbed of her cubs, I will attack them and rip them open. Like a lion I will devour them; a wild animal will tear them apart.
verses.9: "You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against me, against your helper.
verses.10: Where is your king, that he may save you? Where are your rulers in all your towns, of whom you said, 'Give me a king and princes'?
verses.11: So in my anger I gave you a king, and in my wrath I took him away.
verses.12: The guilt of Ephraim is stored up, his sins are kept on record.
verses.13: Pains as of a woman in childbirth come to him, but he is a child without wisdom; when the time arrives, he does not come to the opening of the womb.
verses.14: "I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death. Where, O death, are your plagues? Where, O grave, is your destruction? "I will have no compassion,
verses.15: even though he thrives among his brothers. An east wind from the LORD will come, blowing in from the desert; his spring will fail and his well dry up. His storehouse will be plundered of all its treasures.
verses.16: The people of Samaria must bear their guilt, because they have rebelled against their God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to the ground, their pregnant women ripped open."

verses.1: Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God. Your sins have been your downfall!
verses.2: Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him: "Forgive all our sins and receive us graciously, that we may offer the fruit of our lips.
verses.3: Assyria cannot save us; we will not mount war-horses. We will never again say 'Our gods' to what our own hands have made, for in you the fatherless find compassion."
verses.4: "I will heal their waywardness and love them freely, for my anger has turned away from them.
verses.5: I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily. Like a cedar of Lebanon he will send down his roots;
verses.6: his young shoots will grow. His splendor will be like an olive tree, his fragrance like a cedar of Lebanon.
verses.7: Men will dwell again in his shade. He will flourish like the grain. He will blossom like a vine, and his fame will be like the wine from Lebanon.
verses.8: O Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? I will answer him and care for him. I am like a green pine tree; your fruitfulness comes from me."
verses.9: Who is wise? He will realize these things. Who is discerning? He will understand them. The ways of the LORD are right; the righteous walk in them, but the rebellious stumble in them.

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth during the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah-the vision he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
verses.2: Hear, O peoples, all of you, listen, O earth and all who are in it, that the Sovereign LORD may witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
verses.3: Look! The LORD is coming from his dwelling place; he comes down and treads the high places of the earth.
verses.4: The mountains melt beneath him and the valleys split apart, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.
verses.5: All this is because of Jacob's transgression, because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is Jacob's transgression? Is it not Samaria? What is Judah's high place? Is it not Jerusalem?
verses.6: "Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of rubble, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones into the valley and lay bare her foundations.
verses.7: All her idols will be broken to pieces; all her temple gifts will be burned with fire; I will destroy all her images. Since she gathered her gifts from the wages of prostitutes, as the wages of prostitutes they will again be used."
verses.8: Because of this I will weep and wail; I will go about barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and moan like an owl.
verses.9: For her wound is incurable; it has come to Judah. It has reached the very gate of my people, even to Jerusalem itself.
verses.10: Tell it not in Gath; weep not at all. In Beth Ophrah roll in the dust.
verses.11: Pass on in nakedness and shame, you who live in Shaphir. Those who live in Zaanan will not come out. Beth Ezel is in mourning; its protection is taken from you.
verses.12: Those who live in Maroth writhe in pain, waiting for relief, because disaster has come from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem.
verses.13: You who live in Lachish, harness the team to the chariot. You were the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
verses.14: Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath. The town of Aczib will prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.
verses.15: I will bring a conqueror against you who live in Mareshah. He who is the glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
verses.16: Shave your heads in mourning for the children in whom you delight; make yourselves as bald as the vulture, for they will go from you into exile.

verses.1: Woe to those who plan iniquity, to those who plot evil on their beds! At morning's light they carry it out because it is in their power to do it.
verses.2: They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them. They defraud a man of his home, a fellowman of his inheritance.
verses.3: Therefore, the LORD says: "I am planning disaster against this people, from which you cannot save yourselves. You will no longer walk proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.
verses.4: In that day men will ridicule you; they will taunt you with this mournful song: 'We are utterly ruined; my people's possession is divided up. He takes it from me! He assigns our fields to traitors.'"
verses.5: Therefore you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot.
verses.6: "Do not prophesy," their prophets say. "Do not prophesy about these things; disgrace will not overtake us."
verses.7: Should it be said, O house of Jacob: "Is the Spirit of the LORD angry? Does he do such things?Do not my words do good to him whose ways are upright?
verses.8: Lately my people have risen up like an enemy. You strip off the rich robe from those who pass by without a care, like men returning from battle.
verses.9: You drive the women of my people from their pleasant homes. You take away my blessing from their children forever.
verses.10: Get up, go away! For this is not your resting place, because it is defiled, it is ruined, beyond all remedy.
verses.11: If a liar and deceiver comes and says, 'I will prophesy for you plenty of wine and beer,' he would be just the prophet for this people!
verses.12: "I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in its pasture; the place will throng with people.
verses.13: One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate and go out. Their king will pass through before them, the LORD at their head."

verses.1: Then I said, "Listen, you leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel. Should you not know justice,
verses.2: you who hate good and love evil; who tear the skin from my people and the flesh from their bones;
verses.3: who eat my people's flesh, strip off their skin and break their bones in pieces; who chop them up like meat for the pan, like flesh for the pot?"
verses.4: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. At that time he will hide his face from them because of the evil they have done.
verses.5: This is what the LORD says: "As for the prophets who lead my people astray, if one feeds them, they proclaim 'peace'; if he does not, they prepare to wage war against him.
verses.6: Therefore night will come over you, without visions, and darkness, without divination. The sun will set for the prophets, and the day will go dark for them.
verses.7: The seers will be ashamed and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their faces because there is no answer from God."
verses.8: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression, to Israel his sin.
verses.9: Hear this, you leaders of the house of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and distort all that is right;
verses.10: who build Zion with bloodshed, and Jerusalem with wickedness.
verses.11: Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets tell fortunes for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD and say, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come upon us."
verses.12: Therefore because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, the temple hill a mound overgrown with thickets.

verses.1: In the last days the mountain of the LORD's temple will be established as chief among the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.
verses.2: Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, so that we may walk in his paths." The law will go out from Zion, the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
verses.3: He will judge between many peoples and will settle disputes for strong nations far and wide. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not take up sword against nation, nor will they train for war anymore.
verses.4: Every man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid, for the LORD Almighty has spoken.
verses.5: All the nations may walk in the name of their gods; we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever. The LORD 's Plan
verses.6: "In that day," declares the LORD, "I will gather the lame; I will assemble the exiles and those I have brought to grief.
verses.7: I will make the lame a remnant, those driven away a strong nation. The LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever.
verses.8: As for you, O watchtower of the flock, O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion, the former dominion will be restored to you; kingship will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem."
verses.9: Why do you now cry aloud- have you no king? Has your counselor perished, that pain seizes you like that of a woman in labor?
verses.10: Writhe in agony, O Daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you must leave the city to camp in the open field. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued. There the LORD will redeem you out of the hand of your enemies.
verses.11: But now many nations are gathered against you. They say, "Let her be defiled, let our eyes gloat over Zion!"
verses.12: But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD; they do not understand his plan, he who gathers them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
verses.13: "Rise and thresh, O Daughter of Zion, for I will give you horns of iron; I will give you hoofs of bronze and you will break to pieces many nations." You will devote their ill-gotten gains to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.

verses.7: The remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for man or linger for mankind.
verses.8: The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which mauls and mangles as it goes, and no one can rescue.
verses.9: Your hand will be lifted up in triumph over your enemies, and all your foes will be destroyed.

verses.12: I will destroy your witchcraft and you will no longer cast spells.
verses.13: I will destroy your carved images and your sacred stones from among you; you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
verses.14: I will uproot from among you your Asherah poles and demolish your cities.
verses.15: I will take vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that have not obeyed me."

verses.1: Listen to what the LORD says: "Stand up, plead your case before the mountains; let the hills hear what you have to say.
verses.2: Hear, O mountains, the LORD's accusation; listen, you everlasting foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against his people; he is lodging a charge against Israel.
verses.3: "My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me.
verses.4: I brought you up out of Egypt and redeemed you from the land of slavery. I sent Moses to lead you, also Aaron and Miriam.
verses.5: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD."
verses.6: With what shall I come before the LORD and bow down before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
verses.7: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I offer my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.8: He has showed you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verses.9: Listen! The LORD is calling to the city- and to fear your name is wisdom- "Heed the rod and the One who appointed it.
verses.10: Am I still to forget, O wicked house, your ill-gotten treasures and the short ephah, which is accursed?
verses.11: Shall I acquit a man with dishonest scales, with a bag of false weights?
verses.12: Her rich men are violent; her people are liars and their tongues speak deceitfully.
verses.13: Therefore, I have begun to destroy you, to ruin you because of your sins.
verses.14: You will eat but not be satisfied; your stomach will still be empty. You will store up but save nothing, because what you save I will give to the sword.
verses.15: You will plant but not harvest; you will press olives but not use the oil on yourselves, you will crush grapes but not drink the wine.
verses.16: You have observed the statutes of Omri and all the practices of Ahab's house, and you have followed their traditions. Therefore I will give you over to ruin and your people to derision; you will bear the scorn of the nations. "

verses.3: "My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me.
verses.4: I brought you up out of Egypt and redeemed you from the land of slavery. I sent Moses to lead you, also Aaron and Miriam.
verses.5: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may know the righteous acts of the LORD."
verses.6: With what shall I come before the LORD and bow down before the exalted God? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
verses.7: Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I offer my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
verses.8: He has showed you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verses.9: Listen! The LORD is calling to the city- and to fear your name is wisdom- "Heed the rod and the One who appointed it.
verses.10: Am I still to forget, O wicked house, your ill-gotten treasures and the short ephah, which is accursed?
verses.11: Shall I acquit a man with dishonest scales, with a bag of false weights?
verses.12: Her rich men are violent; her people are liars and their tongues speak deceitfully.
verses.13: Therefore, I have begun to destroy you, to ruin you because of your sins.
verses.14: You will eat but not be satisfied; your stomach will still be empty. You will store up but save nothing, because what you save I will give to the sword.
verses.15: You will plant but not harvest; you will press olives but not use the oil on yourselves, you will crush grapes but not drink the wine.
verses.16: You have observed the statutes of Omri and all the practices of Ahab's house, and you have followed their traditions. Therefore I will give you over to ruin and your people to derision; you will bear the scorn of the nations. "

verses.1: What misery is mine! I am like one who gathers summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster of grapes to eat, none of the early figs that I crave.
verses.2: The godly have been swept from the land; not one upright man remains. All men lie in wait to shed blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
verses.3: Both hands are skilled in doing evil; the ruler demands gifts, the judge accepts bribes, the powerful dictate what they desire- they all conspire together.
verses.4: The best of them is like a brier, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen has come, the day God visits you. Now is the time of their confusion.
verses.5: Do not trust a neighbor; put no confidence in a friend. Even with her who lies in your embrace be careful of your words.
verses.6: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises up against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law- a man's enemies are the members of his own household.
verses.7: But as for me, I watch in hope for the LORD, I wait for God my Savior; my God will hear me.
verses.8: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
verses.9: Because I have sinned against him, I will bear the LORD's wrath, until he pleads my case and establishes my right. He will bring me out into the light; I will see his righteousness.
verses.10: Then my enemy will see it and will be covered with shame, she who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will see her downfall; even now she will be trampled underfoot like mire in the streets.
verses.11: The day for building your walls will come, the day for extending your boundaries.
verses.12: In that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, even from Egypt to the Euphrates and from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
verses.13: The earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the result of their deeds.
verses.14: Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, which lives by itself in a forest, in fertile pasturelands. Let them feed in Bashan and Gilead as in days long ago.
verses.15: "As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show them my wonders."
verses.16: Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their power. They will lay their hands on their mouths and their ears will become deaf.
verses.17: They will lick dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their dens; they will turn in fear to the LORD our God and will be afraid of you.
verses.18: Who is a God like you, who pardons sin and forgives the transgression of the remnant of his inheritance? You do not stay angry forever but delight to show mercy.
verses.19: You will again have compassion on us; you will tread our sins underfoot and hurl all our iniquities into the depths of the sea.
verses.20: You will be true to Jacob, and show mercy to Abraham, as you pledged on oath to our fathers in days long ago.

verses.1: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.2: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his foes and maintains his wrath against his enemies.
verses.3: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will not leave the guilty unpunished. His way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and clouds are the dust of his feet.
verses.4: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither and the blossoms of Lebanon fade.
verses.5: The mountains quake before him and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at his presence, the world and all who live in it.
verses.6: Who can withstand his indignation? Who can endure his fierce anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; the rocks are shattered before him.
verses.7: The LORD is good, a refuge in times of trouble. He cares for those who trust in him,
verses.8: but with an overwhelming flood he will make an end of Nineveh; he will pursue his foes into darkness.
verses.9: Whatever they plot against the LORD he will bring to an end; trouble will not come a second time.
verses.10: They will be entangled among thorns and drunk from their wine; they will be consumed like dry stubble.
verses.11: From you, O Nineveh, has one come forth who plots evil against the LORD and counsels wickedness.
verses.12: This is what the LORD says: "Although they have allies and are numerous, they will be cut off and pass away. Although I have afflicted you, O Judah, I will afflict you no more.
verses.13: Now I will break their yoke from your neck and tear your shackles away."
verses.14: The LORD has given a command concerning you, Nineveh: "You will have no descendants to bear your name. I will destroy the carved images and cast idols that are in the temple of your gods. I will prepare your grave, for you are vile."
verses.15: Look, there on the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your festivals, O Judah, and fulfill your vows. No more will the wicked invade you; they will be completely destroyed.

verses.1: The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, during the reign of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah:
verses.2: "I will sweep away everything from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.
verses.3: "I will sweep away both men and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the air and the fish of the sea. The wicked will have only heaps of rubble when I cut off man from the face of the earth," declares the LORD.
verses.4: "I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place every remnant of Baal, the names of the pagan and the idolatrous priests-
verses.5: those who bow down on the roofs to worship the starry host, those who bow down and swear by the LORD and who also swear by Molech,
verses.6: those who turn back from following the LORD and neither seek the LORD nor inquire of him.
verses.7: Be silent before the Sovereign LORD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated those he has invited.
verses.8: On the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the princes and the king's sons and all those clad in foreign clothes.
verses.9: On that day I will punish all who avoid stepping on the threshold, who fill the temple of their gods with violence and deceit.
verses.10: "On that day," declares the LORD, "a cry will go up from the Fish Gate, wailing from the New Quarter, and a loud crash from the hills.
verses.11: Wail, you who live in the market district; all your merchants will be wiped out, all who trade with silver will be ruined.
verses.12: At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps and punish those who are complacent, who are like wine left on its dregs, who think, 'The LORD will do nothing, either good or bad.'
verses.13: Their wealth will be plundered, their houses demolished. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink the wine.
verses.14: "The great day of the LORD is near- near and coming quickly. Listen! The cry on the day of the LORD will be bitter, the shouting of the warrior there.
verses.15: That day will be a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness,
verses.16: a day of trumpet and battle cry against the fortified cities and against the corner towers.
verses.17: I will bring distress on the people and they will walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust and their entrails like filth.
verses.18: Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the LORD's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole world will be consumed, for he will make a sudden end of all who live in the earth."

verses.3: Why do you make me look at injustice? Why do you tolerate wrong? Destruction and violence are before me; there is strife, and conflict abounds.
verses.4: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails. The wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
verses.5: "Look at the nations and watch- and be utterly amazed. For I am going to do something in your days that you would not believe, even if you were told.
verses.6: I am raising up the Babylonians, that ruthless and impetuous people, who sweep across the whole earth to seize dwelling places not their own.
verses.7: They are a feared and dreaded people; they are a law to themselves and promote their own honor.
verses.8: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves at dusk. Their cavalry gallops headlong; their horsemen come from afar. They fly like a vulture swooping to devour;
verses.9: they all come bent on violence. Their hordes advance like a desert wind and gather prisoners like sand.
verses.10: They deride kings and scoff at rulers. They laugh at all fortified cities; they build earthen ramps and capture them.
verses.11: Then they sweep past like the wind and go on- guilty men, whose own strength is their god."

verses.1: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. On shigionoth.
verses.2: LORD, I have heard of your fame; I stand in awe of your deeds, O LORD. Renew them in our day, in our time make them known; in wrath remember mercy.
verses.3: God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah His glory covered the heavens and his praise filled the earth.
verses.4: His splendor was like the sunrise; rays flashed from his hand, where his power was hidden.
verses.5: Plague went before him; pestilence followed his steps.
verses.6: He stood, and shook the earth; he looked, and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains crumbled and the age-old hills collapsed. His ways are eternal.
verses.7: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress, the dwellings of Midian in anguish.
verses.8: Were you angry with the rivers, O LORD? Was your wrath against the streams? Did you rage against the sea when you rode with your horses and your victorious chariots?
verses.9: You uncovered your bow, you called for many arrows. Selah You split the earth with rivers;
verses.10: the mountains saw you and writhed. Torrents of water swept by; the deep roared and lifted its waves on high.
verses.11: Sun and moon stood still in the heavens at the glint of your flying arrows, at the lightning of your flashing spear.
verses.12: In wrath you strode through the earth and in anger you threshed the nations.
verses.13: You came out to deliver your people, to save your anointed one. You crushed the leader of the land of wickedness, you stripped him from head to foot. Selah
verses.14: With his own spear you pierced his head when his warriors stormed out to scatter us, gloating as though about to devour the wretched who were in hiding.
verses.15: You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the great waters.
verses.16: I heard and my heart pounded, my lips quivered at the sound; decay crept into my bones, and my legs trembled. Yet I will wait patiently for the day of calamity to come on the nation invading us.
verses.17: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though there are no sheep in the pen and no cattle in the stalls,
verses.18: yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will be joyful in God my Savior.
verses.19: The Sovereign LORD is my strength; he makes my feet like the feet of a deer, he enables me to go on the heights. For the director of music. On my stringed instruments.
